page.layout: One column of running text. Above it, the running head "ad Lectorem." Below the last line, at the right, a catchword "ẽ". No page number, no margin notes.

p.i: autem obscura facis igniculis tam late patentem, sefeq; iamdudum per orbem nostrum diffundentem splendorem illustrare, aut ἡλίῳ τὸ Φῶς δανείζειν, sed non pudebit praestare quod tam liquentibus causis recu-sare non potui. Ignoscet facile qui noscit.

Habes ergo, vel me tacente, Amice lector, librum multò quàm antea castigatiorem, innumeris mendis ita olim scatentem, ut de eo dicere liceret, quod Simonem de Homericis scriptis Arato dixisse ferunt, depravatum, scilicet ab his qui emendare vole-bant, ut imperiti Chirurgi vulnus faciunt dum medentur. Solius erat CASAVBONI tam altos errores ingenij acie eruere, tam foedos critica spongia elucere, & Philosophum

page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s throughout. The Greek "Φῶς" and "δανείζειν" are copied as seen; the accents on "δανείζειν" are uncertain. The catchword "ẽ" at the foot is read from a small mark and is doubtful. Small caps "CASAVBONI" are set in capitals. The Ignoscet initial is read as I, though the printed capital resembles J. The "recu-sare" and "vole-bant" hyphens are printed line-end hyphens.
